title: Mall-O-Ween Friday, two Redondo candy routes Saturday, Día de los Muertos Sunday
intro: Halloween is on a Saturday this year. Friday has indoor trick-or-treat at Del Amo and candy on the Redondo Pier. Saturday you can do Harbor Haunts on the boardwalk at noon, El Segundo's Main Street party, then Riviera Village at 3. Sunday is the last night of the Jack O'Lanterns and Long Beach's free Día de los Muertos festival. We left parking, food, and prices blank unless an official page confirmed them.

picks.name: Mall-O-Ween Trick-or-Treat at Del Amo
picks.address: Del Amo Fashion Center, 3525 W. Carson Street (enter just south of Carson St near Macy's Men & Home)
picks.cost_math: Free (City of Torrance). Pre-registration required (link on the city page). Candy while supplies last.
picks.parking: Del Amo Fashion Center lots. The city page does not list a fee.
picks.food: Mall restaurants. No event food listed.
picks.why: Indoor trick-or-treat at the mall the night before Halloween, rain or shine. Register first.

picks.name: Halloween on the Redondo Beach Pier
picks.when: Friday, October 30, 5:00–8:00 p.m. (trick-or-treating 5:00–6:00 p.m. while supplies last)
picks.cost_math: Free and open to the public (official). Parking: Pier or Plaza parking structure, $2.25/hr (City of Redondo Beach) → about $6.75 for 3 hours.
picks.parking: Pier Parking Structure (100 W. Torrance Blvd) or the Plaza Parking Structure: $2.25/hr, pay-by-space (City of Redondo Beach waterfront parking page).
picks.food: Pier restaurants. No event food listed.
picks.why: Trick-or-treat with pier businesses, then a magic show, music, and crafts by the water. Free, weather permitting.

picks.name: Harbor Haunts: Trick or Treat by the Sea
picks.address: International Boardwalk at the Redondo Beach Pier (check in at the north end, above the Paddle House)
picks.cost_math: Free (King Harbor Association). Organizers suggest the King Harbor Parking Lot; its rate isn't on the event page. The city's Pier/Plaza structures and Marina lot near the boardwalk charge $2.25/hr.
picks.parking: Suggested: King Harbor Parking Lot (rate not listed on the event page). City options near the boardwalk: Pier/Plaza structures or the Redondo Beach Marina lot (181 N. Harbor Dr), $2.25/hr (city waterfront parking page).
picks.food: Boardwalk and pier restaurants. No event food listed.
picks.why: Daytime shop-to-shop trick-or-treat on the boardwalk with a dance party, crafts, a photo booth, and Halloween Bingo for prizes. Rain or shine.

picks.name: El Segundo Halloween Frolic
picks.cost_math: Activity wristbands are $10 pre-sale at the Clubhouse and Joslyn Center (City of El Segundo). If both kids get one: $20. The city doesn't say whether adults need wristbands or list a day-of price. Parking not listed.
picks.parking: The city announcement does not list parking. Expect downtown street parking.
picks.food: Food at the event (city announcement). Prices not listed.
picks.why: El Segundo shuts down Main Street for bounce houses, crafts, games, and music. A small-town daytime Halloween block party.

picks.name: Riviera Village Halloween Trick or Treat
picks.when: Saturday, October 31, 3:00–8:00 p.m. (candy until 6:00 p.m. while supplies last)
picks.address: Riviera Village, Catalina Ave (Avenue I to S. Elena St)
picks.cost_math: Free street trick-or-treat. Cashless paid parking at Plaza Riviera (1611 S Catalina Ave) and the Mira Mar Park lot; rates not listed.
picks.parking: Triangle lot between Avenida Del Norte and S. Elena, street spots, cashless paid parking at Plaza Riviera (1611 S Catalina Ave; Apple Pay/Google Pay recommended), and a paid lot at Mira Mar Park (201 Paseo de la Playa). Rates not listed.
picks.food: Village restaurants; stay for dinner (official). No event food listed.
picks.why: Halloween afternoon on a car-free Catalina Ave, the South Bay's big street trick-or-treat. Go early, because candy runs out at 6.

picks.price_text: From $37.07 (Oct 30–31) / $26.77 (Nov 1) per ticket incl. fees; dynamic pricing
picks.name: Magic of the Jack O'Lanterns (final weekend)
picks.when: Friday, October 30–Sunday, November 1 (Sunday is closing night; timed tickets, hours vary by date)
picks.address: South Coast Botanic Garden, 26300 Crenshaw Blvd
picks.cost_math: Dynamic pricing. The lowest listed ticket on the Zentix calendar is $37.07 Fri–Sat and $26.77 Sun, including fees → at least ~$148 Fri/Sat or ~$107 Sun for 4 if all four tickets got that price. Adult tickets usually cost more than kids'. Parking add-on: $10 standard (off-site lot with shuttle) or $25 preferred at the Garden, sold online.
picks.parking: Buy parking with tickets (online only): Standard $10 at 25851 Hawthorne Blvd, Rolling Hills Estates, with a shuttle; Preferred $25 at the Garden (limited).
picks.food: Food and drinks on site, plus a make-your-own s'mores area. Cashless (cards only).
picks.why: Last call for the carved-pumpkin trail, plus a Fun Zone with a bounce pad and slides. Sunday is the cheapest night left.

picks.name: Long Beach Día de los Muertos Festival
picks.cost_math: Free and open to the public (City of Long Beach). The city page does not list parking.
picks.parking: The city page does not list parking. Expect downtown Long Beach lots and garages.
picks.food: Food vendors expected (the city recruited vendors). Prices not listed.
picks.why: Long Beach's 10th annual Día de los Muertos is back as a full festival on the downtown waterfront, with performances and vendors.

picks.name: Snow Play and Santa Day
picks.address: Christ Lutheran Church & School, 28850 S. Western Ave
picks.cost_math: 2 kids × $30 = $60 (Eventbrite ticket page linked from the school's event page). No adult price listed. Free parking listed. No refunds.
picks.parking: Free parking (Eventbrite ticket page linked from the school's event page).
picks.food: The organizer mentions food; prices not listed.
picks.why: Real snow and a sledding ramp in RPV, plus Santa, Elsa and Anna, a bounce house, and crafts. Check in at the side gate for your kid's wristband.

picks.price_text: $10 per guest (cash); free for Peninsula veterans
picks.name: Rancho Palos Verdes Veterans Day Breakfast & Ceremony
picks.when: Wednesday, November 11, 9:00–11:00 a.m. (RSVP by Friday, October 30)
picks.address: Ken Dyda Civic Center, 30940 Hawthorne Blvd
picks.cost_math: $10 per person for attendees who aren't Peninsula veterans, cash only, paid at the event → 4 × $10 = $40. Free for Peninsula veterans (RPV, Rolling Hills Estates, Rolling Hills, PV Estates). RSVP online by Oct 30. Parking not listed.
picks.parking: The city notice does not list parking.
picks.why: A Veterans Day morning with hot breakfast, music, and remarks from local youth organizations. A good way to show kids what the day is for. RSVP by Friday.

picks.price_text: $33 adult (16+), $18 child (3–15), under 3 free; + $1.33 booking fee per ticket
picks.name: Tinker Bell's Neverland: An Illuminated Adventure (opening weekend)
picks.when: Opens Friday, November 13; nightly 5:30–8:30 p.m. through January 3 (closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day)
picks.address: South Coast Botanic Garden, 26300 Crenshaw Blvd
picks.cost_math: 2 adults × $33 + 2 kids (3–15) × $18 = $102, plus a $1.33 booking fee per ticket ($5.32) → $107.32 (Fever, fixed date/time). Under 3 free ($1.33 booking fee still applies). Parking is extra: on-site parking for purchase, price not listed.
picks.parking: On-site parking available for purchase (official/Fever). Price not listed.
picks.food: Hot cocoa, snacks, and drinks for purchase.
picks.why: A new Peter Pan–themed light walk at the botanic garden, about 60–90 minutes. Stroller-friendly, no strobe lights. Opening weekend is the weekend after next.

picks.name: Magic Model Sugar Skulls at Hermosa Beach Library
picks.cost_math: Free library program (no fee listed). Parking not listed.
picks.parking: The library page does not list parking.
picks.why: A free Día de los Muertos sugar-skull decorating session for kids. An easy Halloween-morning stop before the candy runs.
picks.age_gate: Ages 5–12 with a parent or caregiver

picks.name: Wilson Park Train Rides (Southern California Live Steamers)
picks.when: Sunday, November 1, 11:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m. (public rides first Sunday and third Saturday)
picks.cost_math: No fare for public rides; the club runs on donations at the station.
picks.parking: Wilson Park lots. The club site does not list parking.
picks.why: Volunteer-run miniature trains on the first Sunday of the month. The club's website was down Wednesday morning, so check its Facebook before you go.
picks.age_gate: Riders must be 32" tall and walk on their own; no infants; kids ride with an adult
